3.text: apart, or the woman will grow sickly, and soon become sterile. A like result

4.text: is represented as following the infraction of other taboos connected with

6.text: this interdiction, and have intercourse with their wives during the time of the

7.text: menses. Among the Maritime people, both the Chukchee and the Asiatic

8.text: Eskimo, the taboo concerning the menses is much stronger. A woman at

9.text: the time of her courses must carefully avoid even to approach her husband.

10.text: Even her breath is considered as impure: should it touch her husband or any

11.text: other man; it would contaminate him, and destroy his chance in sea-hunting

12.text: pursuits. He would even run the risk of being drowned at sea. In these

13.text: latter details we see a resemblance to the ideas of the American Eskimo.

14.text: The chief taboo among the Maritime people, both Chukchee and Eskimo,

15.text: is a strict prohibition against the use of wood for fuel during the winter.

16.text: The time during which this taboo is in force is marked by the going-away

17.text: and the coming-back of sea-fowl, since all other indications are not sure. The

18.text: cold continues almost throughout the year, and the ice-floes change their

19.text: position with a change of winds, and may be drifted off from shore even in

20.text: the middle of winter. The reason given for the taboo is, that the smell of

21.text: the smoke will “frighten away” the seals and the walruses. A coal-fire is

27.text: Another very important taboo refers to the precaution relative to scraping

28.text: skins, and especially to rubbing them with alder, when the carcass of a killed

29.text: whale is hauled to the shore. Any use of alder is forbidden till the whole

30.text: amount of meat and blubber is stored away by the villagers. A woman who

31.text: has her hands stained with alder-juice makes the “noble guest” suffer. If she
31.note: printed curly closing quote; machine text had a straight closing quote, per §1/§5.6

32.text: washes her hands in sea-water, she causes all the whales to leave the shore.

33.text: The same proscription existed among the Yukaghir of the Lower Kolyma

35.text: Women must take no part whatever in the preparations for the hunt of

36.text: wild reindeer; for instance, it is forbidden to send a woman to fetch a forgotten

37.text: object. While on the watch for wild reindeer, it is forbidden to call it by its

38.text: name, or to point toward it with a finger. It is forbidden to cook seal-meat,

39.text: fish, and reindeer-meat in the same pot while the hunt is going on and all

40.text: these are fresh from the slaughter. When taken from the storehouse, the

41.text: various kinds of meat may be cooked indiscriminately in the same pot.
